definitions.explanation: The undergraduate medical faculty at a Japanese university, where students train to become doctors. Notoriously competitive to enter and requires six years of study.

examples.japanese: {医学部|いがくぶ}に{合格|ごうかく}した。
examples.english: I passed the entrance exam for medical school.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{東京大学|とうきょうだいがく}の{医学部|いがくぶ}に{在籍|ざいせき}している。
examples.english: She is enrolled in the medical school at the University of Tokyo.

examples.japanese: {医学部|いがくぶ}は{他|た}の{学部|がくぶ}と{違|ちが}い、{六年間|ろくねんかん}の{課程|かてい}となっている。
examples.english: Unlike other faculties, medical school is a six-year program.

notes:
{医学|いがく} (medicine, medical science) + {部|ぶ} (faculty, department). In Japan, medicine is studied at the undergraduate level as a faculty of a university, not in a separate graduate school as in the US.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {医学部|いがくぶ}に{入|はい}る: to enter medical school
- {医学部|いがくぶ}{受験|じゅけん}: medical school entrance exam
- {医学部|いがくぶ}{生|せい}: medical student (= {医学生|いがくせい})
- {国立|こくりつ}{医学部|いがくぶ}: national-university medical school

CULTURAL NOTE:
Getting into {医学部|いがくぶ} is one of the most competitive academic challenges in Japan, with very high entrance-exam hurdles. Becoming a doctor ({医師|いし}) requires completing the six-year program and passing the national licensing exam.

RELATED FACULTIES:
- {歯学部|しがくぶ}: faculty of dentistry
- {薬学部|やくがくぶ}: faculty of pharmacy
- {看護学部|かんごがくぶ}: faculty of nursing
